sections: Why convert WEBP to PNG?

list: Open images saved from websites in apps that do not accept WebP, such as older versions of Photoshop, Word or Windows Photo Viewer.
Keep transparency – PNG supports full alpha, just like WebP.
Edit without further quality loss: PNG is lossless, so repeated saves do not add artefacts.
Upload to forms and print services that only accept PNG or JPG.

sections: Converting a lossy WebP to PNG cannot restore detail that WebP compression already removed, but it stops any further loss. Expect the PNG to be larger – often 2–5× for photos – because PNG stores every pixel exactly.
Options explained

list: **Quality** – only affects lossy formats; PNG output is lossless.
**Background colour** – used when the output is JPG, to fill transparent areas (white by default).
**Max width** – scales larger images down proportionally; leave empty to keep the original size.
**Make white background transparent** – for PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF and ICO output, turns near-white pixels transparent, useful for logos on white.

sections: Is WEBP to PNG conversion lossless?
PNG stores pixels exactly, so the conversion adds no new compression artefacts. Detail already lost in a lossy WEBP cannot be brought back; the PNG will look exactly like the WEBP you started with.
About the WEBP and PNG formats

WebP was released by Google in 2010, based on the VP8 video codec. One format covers lossy photos, lossless graphics, transparency and animation. Google reports lossy WebP files 25–34% smaller than comparable JPEGs.

PNG was created in the mid-1990s as a patent-free replacement for GIF. It compresses losslessly with the same algorithm as ZIP, so files are exact copies of the pixels – perfect for screenshots, diagrams and logos, but large for photographs.
Convert many images at once

Select or drop as many WEBP files as you like. They are converted one after another on your device and packed into a single ZIP for download. Because nothing is uploaded, batch speed depends only on your computer or phone – typically a fraction of a second per photo on a laptop.
Convert WEBP to PNG on Windows, Mac, iPhone and Android

There is nothing to install: open this page in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. On iPhone and iPad, choose images from Photos or Files and save the result to Files; on Android, results go to Downloads. On a PC or MacBook, you can drag files straight from a folder. Built-in apps can sometimes export PNG too, but a browser converter is the same on every device and handles batches.

Cutting machines follow vector paths, so they need SVG (or DXF) files rather than PNG. For a single-layer cut, choose **2 colours** so the design becomes solid black shapes on white, and *Smooth* detail to drop specks that would turn into tiny cuts. Upload the SVG in Cricut Design Space with *Upload → Upload image*, then check the cut preview: every closed shape becomes a cut line. Use *Weld* or *Attach* in Design Space to keep separate pieces together. For multi-colour layered vinyl, use 4–8 colours; each colour becomes a separate group you can assign to its own layer.
PNG to SVG in Inkscape or Illustrator vs online

Inkscape (*Path → Trace Bitmap*) and Illustrator (*Image Trace*) offer fine control over thresholds, corners and noise, and are the right choice for professional logo redraws. They take time to learn and install. This converter gives you a good first trace in seconds, on any device, without uploading client artwork. You can always open the SVG in Inkscape or Illustrator afterwards to refine nodes, merge shapes or change colours.
Limitations of automatic tracing

list: Photos become poster-like art with thousands of paths and large files – keep photos as PNG, JPG or WebP.
Text in the image is traced as shapes, not editable text; retype it in a design app if needed.
Very thin lines may break up; trace at a larger size or choose High detail.
Gradients are approximated with bands of flat colour.
Huge images are scaled to about 1,000 px (1,600 px in High detail) for tracing, then output at the original dimensions.
Soft shadows and glows turn into stepped rings of colour; remove them from the artwork first if you can.
JPG-compressed sources add speckles around edges – start from the original PNG where possible.

sections: Is PNG to SVG conversion free here?

Yes. There are no limits on the number of images, no daily quota, no watermark and no account. Tracing runs on your own device with the open-source ImageTracer library, so there is no server cost and no reason to restrict you – the only limit is your device's memory for extremely large images. Batch tracing also works: drop several PNGs and download all the SVGs together as one ZIP, each traced with the same colour and detail settings, which is ideal for converting a whole icon set in a single pass.
Checking and using your SVG

Open the downloaded SVG in your browser to see it at any zoom level. In a website, use it in an tag or inline it to style colours with CSS. In Word and PowerPoint (Microsoft 365), insert it as a picture – it stays sharp when resized. For print, most print shops accept SVG or will ask for PDF; convert with a design app or use [Image to PDF](/image-to-pdf/) for a pixel version.
Worked example: a café logo for signage

A café owner has only a 600 × 600 px PNG of the logo, but the sign maker needs a vector file for a 2-metre sign. Drop the PNG, choose 8 colours (the logo has a dark brown, a cream and an orange accent plus their anti-aliased edges), tick *Make white background transparent* and keep *Normal* detail. Convert, then open the SVG in the browser and zoom to 800%: the edges stay smooth instead of turning into blocks. The sign maker can import the SVG straight into their software, or open it in Inkscape to clean a couple of small nodes. Total time: under a minute, with the artwork never leaving the computer.

sections: SVG is usually the most convenient starting point: most design and CAD tools import it and can export the other formats if a supplier insists on one.
Keeping SVG file size small

A trace with many colours and small details can contain thousands of paths. To keep files light for websites: reduce the number of colours, choose *Smooth* detail to drop tiny specks, crop the image tightly before tracing, and avoid tracing photos. For web use you can also run the result through an SVG optimiser such as SVGO, which removes redundant data without changing the look.
Who uses PNG to SVG conversion

list: **Small businesses** turning a logo into a vector for signs, vehicle wraps and embroidery.
**Crafters** making Cricut and Silhouette cut files for vinyl, iron-on and paper.
**Web developers** replacing blurry PNG icons with crisp, scalable SVGs.
**Laser-engraving and CNC hobbyists** creating paths from drawings.
**Teachers and students** vectorising diagrams for slides and posters.

steps: Start with the biggest, cleanest PNG you have.
Crop and, if needed, remove the background.
Pick colours: 2 for cut files, 8–16 for logos.
Choose detail: Normal first; High for fine lines, Smooth for cleaner shapes.
Convert and open the SVG in your browser at high zoom.
If it looks noisy, lower colours or pick Smooth and run again.

sections: Because the original PNG is never changed and every run takes seconds, it is quick to try two or three settings and keep the best one.
Can I change PNG to SVG just by renaming?

No. Renaming *logo.png* to *logo.svg* does not change the content – apps will refuse to open it or show an error. Some online tools also just embed the PNG pixels inside an SVG wrapper, which still pixelates when enlarged. A real conversion must trace the pixels into vector paths, which is what this tool does; you can check by opening the SVG in a text editor and seeing *path* elements rather than a long base64 image.
Make the background transparent

Tick *Make white background transparent* before converting and white areas become empty rather than white shapes – essential for logos that will sit on coloured backgrounds, and for cut files where you do not want a big rectangle around the design.
Privacy

Images are decoded and converted inside your browser using the built-in image engine (and WebAssembly encoders for AVIF and tracing for SVG). Nothing is uploaded or stored on a server, there is no account, and the page keeps working offline once loaded – handy for personal photos, ID scans and client artwork.

sections: Is GIF to PNG conversion lossless?
PNG stores pixels exactly, so the conversion adds no new compression artefacts. Detail already lost in a lossy GIF cannot be brought back; the PNG will look exactly like the GIF you started with.
About the GIF and PNG formats
GIF was introduced by CompuServe in 1987. It is limited to 256 colours per frame but supports simple animation and on/off transparency, which is why it remains popular for short loops and reactions.

PNG was created in the mid-1990s as a patent-free replacement for GIF. It compresses losslessly with the same algorithm as ZIP, so files are exact copies of the pixels – perfect for screenshots, diagrams and logos, but large for photographs.
